### American Vanguard Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 9, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/206980792/files/doc_news/American-Vanguard-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


Strategic Deals in Quarter Expand U.S. Product PortfolioConsolidation Driving Manufacturing Efficiency GainsEl Nino and Geopolitics Pressure Global Agricultural Markets


**IRVINE, CA /[ACCESS Newswire](https://www.accessnewswire.com/) / November 9, 2026 /** American Vanguard Corporation, a diversified specialty and agricultural products company that develops, manufactures, and markets solutions for crop protection and nutrition, turf and ornamental management and commercial pest control, today reported financial results for the third quarter and nine-months ended September 30, 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights - versus Third Quarter 2025**


- Net sales of $108 million as compared to $119 million;
- Gross profit margin of 24%, as compared to 29%;
- Operating loss of $8.0 million, as compared to operating loss of $6.5 million;
- Net loss of $17.7 million, as compared to $12.4 million;
- Breakeven Adjusted EBITDA\[1\] as compared to $8.3 million;
- EPS of ($0.61), as compared to ($0.43)
- Revise Full-Year Outlook; Adjusted EBITDA $36 million to $40 million on Sales of $500 million to $530 million


Dak Kaye, CEO of American Vanguard, stated, "Our actions are taking hold, and the progress we are making across American Vanguard continues to build, even as market conditions remain difficult, particularly outside the U.S., where El Niño is materially impacting our business this year. In the U.S., our largest and most important market, we continue to outperform our peers in a challenging environment. The cost actions we took in the first half, including the rationalization of our Los Angeles facility and the relocation of our headquarters are beginning to deliver operational savings. In the near term, however, those savings have been more than offset by a sharp rise in diesel and other transportation costs arising from instability in the Middle East. We are working to recover gross margins through commercial actions."


Mr. Kaye continued, "Importantly, we are building a new product engine that we believe will drive growth over the next several years. At the end of the third quarter, we acquired four U.S. brands and registrations from Syngenta® and entered into a distribution agreement with Sipcam Agro, which together meaningfully expand our portfolio. Combined with our pipeline of new product launches, these additions support our goal of driving $100 million in annualized revenue from new products by 2030. I am also pleased that we have further strengthened our leadership team in the quarter with the additions of Matt Horwath as Chief Financial Officer, and Hermann Castro, Senior Vice President of Marketing and Business Development, to drive new product development and Mark Helt as President of U.S. Crop. Our focus is the same in every market: stay close to our customers, provide service and solutions, and control what we can control."


Matt Horwath, Chief Financial Officer, stated, "We began to see progress this quarter in terms of lower operating costs and improved manufacturing efficiencies as a result of actions taken earlier this year. However, this progress was more than offset in the quarter by the effects of negative operating leverage, driven by lower international sales and higher raw material and transportation costs. Net trade working capital improved by $22 million, or 14%, versus the prior year period. Higher pre-payments in the quarter, which increase by 44% year-over-year, demonstrate customer confidence and bode well for revenue in the 2027 planting season."

**About American Vanguard**


American Vanguard Corporation is a diversified specialty and agriculture products company that develops and markets products for crop protection and management, turf and ornamentals management, and public health. Over the past 20 years, through product and business acquisitions, the Company has significantly expanded its operations and now has more than 1,000 product registrations worldwide. To learn more about the Company, please reference[www.american-vanguard.com](https://pr.report/td88) .

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to providing results that are determined in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAP), we present Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses, which are non-GAAP financial measures. These measures should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative to GAAP measures such as net income, or diluted earnings per share, as applicable, or other financial statement data presented in our financial statements as an indicator of our financial performance or liquidity.


We define EBITDA as net (loss) income, adjusted for depreciation and amortization, provision for income taxes and interest expense. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA as further adjusted for stock compensation expense and for certain items management believe are not reflective of the underlying operations of our business, including but not limited to the exclusion of charges that are considered by management to be unusual and not representative of the Company's underlying performance and future prospects. In 2026 and 2025 that included non-recurring expenses. The resulting Adjusted EBITDA measure is aligned with the Company's metric for its credit facility agreement in the applicable periods.


We define Adjusted operating expense as operating expenses as further adjusted for stock compensation expense and for certain items management believe are not reflective of the underlying operations of our business, including but not limited to the exclusion of charges that are considered by management to be unusual and not representative of the Company's underlying performance and future prospects as well as the amortization expense for intangibles assets related to acquired product lines.


We use Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses to assess the operating results and effectiveness and efficiency of our business. We present this non-GAAP financial measure because we believe that investors consider Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses to be an important supplemental measure of performance, and we believe that this measure is frequently used by securities analysts, investors and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in our industry. As the Company continues to work through its transformation efforts, management believes that presenting Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses provides an effective comparison between the Company and its industry peers. Non-GAAP financial measures as reported by us may not be comparable to similarly titled metrics reported by other companies and may not be calculated in the same manner. These measures have limitations as analytical tools, and you should not consider them in isolation or as substitutes for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP.


The Company is not able to provide a reconciliation without unreasonable efforts of its forward-looking guidance related to Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure due to the inherent difficulty in predicting with reasonable certainty the timing and amount of certain items that are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted operating expenses, such as share-based compensation, acquisition-related expenses, and foreign exchange gains or losses, which could be material to the Company's results computed in accordance with GAAP.
